title: Support Dolby Vision (Profile 8) media having HDR10/HLG fallback (on webOS)
body:
Currently, in [MediaBrowser.Model/Entities/MediaStream.cs](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/blob/master/MediaBrowser.Model/Entities/MediaStream.cs#L688C1-L699C1), the GetVideoColorRange function exits as soon as it finds the media file to have HDR10 or HLG data.
This return happens too soon, not accounting for Dolby Vision Profile 8 media that have [both DOVI and HDR10/HLG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolby_Vision#Profiles) data - leading to only HDR10 level playback for DOVI media on my TV with DOVI support.

My approach included adding two new possible enumerations to `VideoRangeType` - `DOVI_with_HDR10_Fallback` and `DOVI_with_HLG_Fallback`, and adding these in wherever i found `VideoRangeType.HDR10 / HLG` or `VideoRangeType.DOVI` in the code. 

--
It seems redundant to have the client send in that they support both `HDR10` and `DOVI_with_HDR10_Fallback`, so I'm open to suggestions on how to better implement this - please do point me towards the files that would need changing as well!
I think the best way would be to add support for multiple VideoRangeTypes, but I'm not sure how/how much would have to change for that.

Another open question is how should the IsHwTonemapAvailable functions in [MediaBrowser.Controller/MediaEncoding/EncodingHelper.cs](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/blob/208b585a3f7d9764c023024b2a14e619464bdc04/MediaBrowser.Controller/MediaEncoding/EncodingHelper.cs#L253C1-L256C76) handle these new video range types? It makes sense to me that if these dovi+hdr files were being processed as just hdr until now and worked fine, we should be able to add them along with the hdr10/hlg support assertion no problem.


I look forward to knowing your thoughts on this. I'll open a PR with the mentioned approach now.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
In fact, reporting this DOVI flag here means that the client MUST support ALL common DOVI Profiles, including but not limited to Profile 5 as well as 7 and 8. An example is mainstream Apple devices, which are Dolby Vision certified.

Otherwise it is enough to report HDR10 and HLG for DOVI content with fallback layer so that Jellyfin does not force transcode them and let the client handle them.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I should clarify why I thought this change was necessary - I'll express my experience upto this point.

On webOS, DoVi will not playback if container is not mp4. So, I added code in jellyfin-web to cause a remux (to fMP4-HLS) if the video range type is DOVI and container is not mp4. That takes care of profile 5 playback there.

However, for profile 8 media, MediaStream.cs will report those files to be HDR10 or HLG instead of DOVI. That means to apply the same fix in jellyfin-web, I'd have to block HDR10/HLG for non-mp4 as well.

If I go ahead and do that, a separate issue remains - [These lines](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/blob/42a7e4cf1a09404eae3f588ba5c6312633bfb2da/Jellyfin.Api/Controllers/DynamicHlsController.cs#L1849-L1852) in DynamicHlsController.cs do not sufficiently detect media that are DoVi Profile 8 - ffprobe will not return the CodecTag data for mkv containers that this block of logic relies on. This leads to the remux (to fMP4-HLS) without the DoVi data being copied.

So to resolve this, we could either go with the approach I imagined here or perhaps find another way to reliably detect DoVi content on any container and use that logic in DynamicHlsController.cs.
(or we could say this is an issue with ffprobe not returning codectag for mkv, and look for fixes there instead)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> If I go ahead and do that, a separate issue remains - [These lines](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/blob/42a7e4cf1a09404eae3f588ba5c6312633bfb2da/Jellyfin.Api/Controllers/DynamicHlsController.cs#L1849-L1852) in DynamicHlsController.cs do not sufficiently detect media that are DoVi Profile 8 - ffprobe will not return the CodecTag data for mkv containers that this block of logic relies on.


The `dvh1` codec tag is specifically for Profile 5 content, while Profile 7 and 8 content are generally tagged as `hvc1`.

`dvh1` is far less compatible than `hvc1` and will easily fail on players that don't support DOVI. So for P7/8, use `hvc1` and pass the DOVI metadata via fMP4 and let the client handle it on its own.

> This leads to the remux (to fMP4-HLS) without the DoVi data being copied.

We have patch to enable this in our FFmpeg.

https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin-ffmpeg/blob/8a12a4cf5c3ae2c0fa4650b5abc99d32252006e6/debian/patches/0033-add-hevc-dovi-sidedata-to-hlsenc.patch#L18

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
No no, I mean that ffprobe, which jellyfin uses to populate the `state.VideoStream.CodecTag` field, does not pick up anything when it looks for that info in DoVi media inside mkv containers.

Here I have an mp4 file that has DoVi content
`v@v:~/Media/Movies$ /lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffprobe "Mystery Box Dolby Vision Profile 5.mp4"`
![image](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/assets/12881174/3d58d560-2db3-4c20-94a9-80d40a959a68)

I'll remux it to mkv using jellyfin-ffmpeg 6. 
`v@v:~/Media/Movies$ /lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffmpeg -i "Mystery Box Dolby Vision Profile 5.mp4" -c copy testmkv2.mkv`
`v@v:~/Media/Movies$ /lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffprobe testmkv2.mkv`
![image](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/assets/12881174/0d13185d-ce4c-4320-8c21-f222357e0159)

If I convert that mkv back to mp4, (need to do `-strict unofficial` here else I don't get dovi playback)
`/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffmpeg -i testmkv2.mkv -c copy -strict unofficial propermp4.mp4`
![image](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/assets/12881174/2bd1553e-0a2a-4a11-840f-658fad108fa1)

Huh, it gives back hev1. I guess it didn't bother me because I'll be direct playing mp4s, so I don't touch the described issue in DynamicHlsController.cs.

--

The issue is that when an mkv file containing DOVI is sent for remuxing (to fMP4-HLS) and the code flow arrives at DynamicHlsController.cs, all the checks to determine if the file is DOVI fail (`VideoRangeType.DOVI` does not happen for DOVI+HDR10 media, and `state.VideoStream.CodecTag` will always be null when working with mkv media because ffprobe does not pick up this field for mkv.). This leads to the file being incorrectly processed as non-DOVI, leading to remux (to fMP4-HLS) without the DoVi data being copied.



tl;dr: 
We have two issues in jellyfin that prevent Dolby Vision playback on webOS (LG TVs) (uses jellyfin-web as client).
1. webOS requires a remux of other containers to mp4 in order to play DOVI content. Without a specific VideoRangeType to uniquely identify HDR10+DOVI, there is no way to instruct the server to not direct play these specific files. Currently these files are recognized simply as HDR10/HLG.
2. As a test, we could disallow all non mp4 containers from direct playing HDR10/HLG on webOS, on the off-chance they actually contain DOVI content (needing a remux). Still, we end up without DOVI as the DynamicHlsController.cs fails to recognize those files as DOVI.

My PR solves both these issues by introducing a new VideoRangeType for this type of media.

I think that might mess with browsers that can do upto HDR10/HLG direct play -- if my browser can playback HDR10, but jellyfin recognizes the fallback-able media as DOVI now and my codecprofile says I can't do DOVI, it would cause a remux for those clients who were enjoying direct play before.


Yup. Right now without any changes on webOS, when a non-mp4 DOVI with fallback appears, it's direct played as fallback (it direct plays as HDR instead of DOVI). When a non-mp4 without fallback appears, it is direct played with green-purple tone.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> Right now without any changes on webOS, when a non-mp4 DOVI with fallback appears, it's direct played as fallback (it direct plays as HDR instead of DOVI).

So it can play the fallback data.

> I think that might mess with browsers that can do upto HDR10/HLG direct play -- if my browser can playback HDR10, but jellyfin recognizes the fallback-able media as DOVI now and my codecprofile says I can't do DOVI, it would cause a remux for those clients who were enjoying direct play before.

Yeah, that could be a problem.
If we add a check for DV profile (has a fallback), we fix non-DOVI clients. But server tries to use direct play whenever possible, and we want it to remux to get full DoVi (literally the opposite).

So the problem is, how to say the server that we prefer to preserve the video range (accept remuxing)?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I'm not sure - do you have any suggestions?

I also request feedback on this PR in the jellyfin server https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/pull/10469/ with my approach to include new VideoRangeTypes for fallback-able media. 

By adding new VideoRangeTypes, webOS can send a codec profile to disallow direct playing of those specific types - leading to remux for webOS and no impact for all other browsers (except one - all users will see this media as "DOVI_with_HDR10_Fallback" in playback info screen instead of "HDR10" currently)

Please let me know if it's a viable solution for the project.

MKV DV5: triggers Dolby Vision **(progression)**
TS DV5: triggers Dolby Vision (same as 10.8)
MP4 DV5: triggers Dolby Vision (same as 10.8)

MKV DV8: triggers HDR (same as 10.8)
TS DV8: triggers HDR **(regression)**
MP4 DV8: triggers HDR **(regression)**

So, something's definitely going on with DV8 files. Loading files in general seems also a tad slower.
